title: Quantum priming echoes: microbench journal
content:
Goal: explore subtle priming strategies (short prefix, interleaved priming, batched soft-primes) to see p95/p99 sensitivity and cold-to-hot ramp across mixed client blend. Wanted a compact name so I could grep logs: "quantum priming" = many tiny priming fragments interleaved between real requests (vs single contiguous prefix).

Setup summary:
- Hardware: 1xA100-40GB (dev cluster), 1xRTX6000 (edge-sim), 4-core CPU proxy box.
- Model: open llama-7B-quant (fp16/4-bit variant), seq len used = 1024 typical, max=2048 for stress run.
- Runtime flags: --batch-timeout 6ms, --kv-cache=on, --prefill-worker=2, --speculative-decode=off (control).
- Workload: 60:40 real-client blend (40% chat-like short ctx 64 tokens, 60% long completion 512 tokens). Poisson arrival with peak qps=420, sustained 220 qps.
- Measurement windows: cold (after 5m idle), warm (after steady 10m @220 qps), burst (sustained 30s at 420 qps).

Experiments run (ordered):
1) Baseline (no priming): measure cold vs warm p95/p99.
2) Contiguous prime (single 32-token prefix) attached every request.
3) Soft-prime batch: attach 8x4-token micro-primes across requests in a burst-aligned manner.
4) Quantum priming: interleave 1-2 token primes randomly across client stream (prob 0.12 per request).
5) KV-cache-only: cache priming responses at proxy layer, no attached tokens (cache-hit sim).

Representative findings (numbers are medians over 5 runs; p99 measured with 99.5th percentile sampling):
- Baseline warm: p50 18ms, p95 64ms, p99 142ms, throughput steady 220 qps. Cold p99 spikes to ~540ms on first few requests (priming load).
- Contiguous prime: p95 increases +12ms relative baseline; p99 increases +35ms. Cold p99 slightly worse (cache fill cost bigger chunk).
- Soft-prime batch: p95 ~ baseline +3ms; p99 +12ms. Better than contiguous for p99, likely due to staggered CPU/GPU overlap.
- Quantum priming: p95 almost identical to baseline (+1-2ms); p99 improved by ~8ms vs baseline in warm state. Cold p99 still spikes but smaller amplitude (peak ~380ms).
- KV-cache-only: best p50/p95 but p99 unstable during burst (cache-miss amplification).

Notes on micro-behaviors observed in traces:
- Quantum priming reduces the prefill burstiness: small primes get absorbed into existing batching window and help keep KV cache warm without creating a huge contiguous prefill.
- Contiguous primes trigger longer single prefill operations that block other small requests; batching aligns badly with our --batch-timeout(6ms).
- Soft-prime batch improves tail by spreading work, but it increases total token cost ~4% (tradeoff).
- KV-cache-only is fragile: any eviction policy mismatch during peak qps leads to amplified p99 tail due to cold-path penalty.

Quick commands (so I can reproduce):
- start workload: scripts/run_poisson_blend.sh --qps 220 --peak 420 --blend 0.6 --seed 42
- runtime flags used: SERVER_OPTS="--batch-timeout=6 --kv-cache=on --prefill-worker=2" \n- trace collect: tcpdump -i eth0 -w /tmp/trace_priming.pcap (then convert to token-level traces via tools/trace2tokens.py)

Rough cost delta (simulated):
- Quantum priming adds ~1.6% token volume (because many primes are 1-2 tokens).
- Soft-prime batch adds ~4%. Contiguous prime adds ~6% due to repeated prefix attachment.
- Tradeoff: quantum priming -> lower p99 for warmed fleets at much lower token cost than contiguous priming.

Open questions / TODOs:
- Tune --batch-timeout: 6ms might be borderline. Try 4ms and 8ms to see sensitivity (TODO: A/B next week).
- Interaction with speculative decode: currently off. Hypothesis: speculative might hide contiguous prefill cost; need to test. (link to PR: github PR 2345 touching speculative pipeline)
- Eviction policy: instrument LRU vs CLOCK to see KV-cache-only fragility. Samir to add eviction telemetry.
- Real-client A/B: run quantum priming as canary on 5% live traffic (requires approvals, risk low but need SLA gating).

Anomalies worth flagging:
- Run 4 (quantum priming) had two outlier p99 events coincident with proxy GC spikes (saw heap compaction at 2026-01-18T14:03). Need to correlate GC logs with token traces.
- On RTX6000 edge-sim box quantum priming didn't help p99 as much (probably because small primes don't amortize kernel startup; investigate kernel hot paths).

Conclusions (working):
- Quantum priming is promising: small token insertions spread across requests warm KV cache and smooth prefill without large contiguous overhead. Good cost/perf tradeoff for steady-state clusters.
- For cold-start heavy fleets (long idle periods) contiguous priming still helps first-response quality/latency in some cases but at higher token cost and tail risk.
- Recommend short-term: run a controlled canary of quantum priming on internal traffic with batch-timeout=6ms, collect p50/p95/p99 over 1w, compare cost delta.

Quick links / refs:
- Slack thread: slack://workspace/priming-experiments (search "quantum priming")
- GH PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/2345
- Jira: INFR-783 (epic for priming experiments)

Scratch notes (unordered):
- If we can do prime-as-spans (attach metadata instead of tokens) could avoid token-count cost — but needs model-side support.
- Possible mixing strategy: quantum primes for warm fleets, soft-prime batch during controlled ramp windows.
- Keep an eye on billing alerts: soft-prime batch increases token cost nonlinearly during peak bursts if primes align badly.

End of journal.
